Open one level at a time. **Hint 1** gives the conceptual direction, **Hint 2** the SQL technique, **Hint 3** the query structure, and the final level is in [`solutions/`](../solutions/).

## M2-E01 · Insert the first artwork

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

INSERT needs three things: the table, the list of columns, and the matching list of values.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

The statement is `INSERT INTO table (column, ...) VALUES (value, ...);`. The n-th value goes into the n-th listed column.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

List all four columns (id, title, accession_number, acquired), then the four values in the same order. Quote the text values, including the accession number.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e01).

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

## M2-E06 · From an imported CSV into the real table

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

`INSERT INTO table (cols) SELECT cols FROM other;` inserts a query's result. The columns must line up.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`NULLIF(x, '')` returns NULL when x is the empty string, otherwise x.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`INSERT INTO "collections" ("title", "accession_number", "acquired") SELECT "title", "accession_number", NULLIF("acquired", '') FROM "temp"; DROP TABLE "temp";`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e06).

## M2-E07 · Delete everything acquired before 1909

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Which column expresses "before 1909"? Ids are a fragile proxy (L787-792).

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` text compare correctly with `<`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`DELETE FROM "collections" WHERE "acquired" < '1909-01-01';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e07).

## M2-E08 · Delete the undated artwork

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Never run a DELETE without a WHERE, unless you really mean every row.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`= NULL` never matches anything.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`DELETE FROM "collections" WHERE "acquired" IS NULL;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e08).

## M2-E09 · Delete an artist the two-step way

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

First remove what *references* the artist, then the artist.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Find the id with a subquery on `artists`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`DELETE FROM "created" WHERE "artist_id" = (SELECT "id" FROM "artists" WHERE "name" = 'Unidentified artist');` then `DELETE FROM "artists" WHERE ...;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e09).

## M2-E10 · Hit the FOREIGN KEY constraint

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

The artist's id is still referenced in `created`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

A plain DELETE with a WHERE on the name.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e10).

## M2-E11 · Let ON DELETE CASCADE do both steps

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

With CASCADE, deleting the referenced row also deletes the referencing rows.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Just delete from `artists`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`DELETE FROM "artists" WHERE "name" = 'Unidentified artist';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e11).

## M2-E12 · Re-attribute an artwork with UPDATE

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

The fact to change lives in the junction table `created`, not in `artists`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`SET "artist_id" = (subquery for Li Yin)` and `WHERE "collection_id" = (subquery for the painting)`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`UPDATE "created" SET "artist_id" = (SELECT "id" FROM "artists" WHERE "name" = 'Li Yin') WHERE "collection_id" = (SELECT "id" FROM "collections" WHERE "title" = 'Farmers Working at Dawn');`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e12).

## M2-E13 · Clean the votes and get four groups

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Fix the systematic problems first, for all rows (no WHERE): whitespace with `trim()`, case with `upper()`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Then fix families of typos with `LIKE` patterns (`%` = any characters; LIKE ignores case), and fix the one-off typos with `=`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Run the GROUP BY after each step. For example `UPDATE "votes" SET "title" = 'FARMERS WORKING AT DAWN' WHERE "title" LIKE 'Fa%';` Then do Imaginative, the `Imagintive` typo, and Profusion.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e13).

## M2-E14 · Triggers that log sales and purchases

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Shape: `CREATE TRIGGER name BEFORE DELETE ON table FOR EACH ROW BEGIN ...; END;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

In a DELETE trigger the row being removed is `OLD`. In an INSERT trigger the new row is `NEW`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Body of sell: `INSERT INTO "transactions" ("title", "action") VALUES (OLD."title", 'sold');`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e14).

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "deleted" INTEGER DEFAULT 0;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

A soft delete is an UPDATE, not a DELETE.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`UPDATE "collections" SET "deleted" = 1 WHERE "title" = 'Farmers Working at Dawn';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#m2-e15).

## D2-05 · NEW in a DELETE trigger

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

In a DELETE, is there a *new* row?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

DELETE triggers see `OLD`, INSERT triggers see `NEW`, and UPDATE triggers see both.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Use `OLD."title"`.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M2.md#d2-05).

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>
